description: Original hand-authored smoke-test corpus, not a hiring-quality benchmark. Splits are by source document.

passages.text: Regularization discourages overly complex models by adding a penalty to the training objective. L2 regularization penalizes squared weights. It can reduce overfitting, but excessive regularization causes underfitting.
A learning rate controls how far an optimizer moves on each update. A very large learning rate may make training unstable. A very small rate can make convergence slow.

questions.question: How does an L2 penalty reduce model overfitting?
What can go wrong when the optimizer takes steps that are too large?

passages.text: Training data is used to fit model parameters. Validation data is used to choose hyperparameters. The test set is reserved for final evaluation after model selection.
Data leakage happens when information unavailable at prediction time influences training or model selection. Related passages from one document should remain in the same split to avoid leakage.

questions.question: Which dataset should select hyperparameters?
Why keep paragraphs from a single source together when splitting data?

passages.text: An embedding maps text to a numeric vector. Semantic retrieval compares a question vector with stored passage vectors, allowing related wording to match even without identical keywords.
Cosine similarity measures the angle between vectors. For unit-normalized embeddings, the dot product equals cosine similarity. Vectors from different embedding models should not be mixed.

questions.question: How can search match passages that use different words?
When does a dot product equal cosine similarity?

passages.text: Hybrid retrieval combines keyword matches and semantic vector matches. Reciprocal rank fusion combines their ranked lists using the sum of one divided by a smoothing constant plus each rank.
A cross-encoder reranker reads the question and a candidate passage together. It scores relevance after initial retrieval. Reranking cannot recover a relevant passage missing from the candidate set.

questions.question: How can keyword and semantic result rankings be combined?
Can a reranker recover evidence that initial search did not retrieve?

passages.text: Recall at k measures the fraction of relevant passages retrieved in the first k results. Mean reciprocal rank averages the inverse rank of the first relevant result across questions.

Precision measures how many predicted positives are correct. Recall measures how many actual positives are recovered. A classifier threshold controls the tradeoff between false positives and false negatives.

questions.question: What metric rewards placing the first useful search result near the top?
What changes the balance between false alarms and missed positives?

passages.text: A durable job queue stores pending work in a database. Workers claim jobs with row locks. SKIP LOCKED lets concurrent workers claim different unlocked rows instead of waiting for one busy row.
Retries should distinguish temporary failures from permanent errors. Exponential backoff increases the delay between attempts. Jitter spreads retries to avoid synchronized request bursts.

questions.question: How do multiple workers avoid waiting on the same locked job?
Why add randomness to retry delays?

passages.text: Optical character recognition converts page images to text. A scanned PDF may need OCR because it contains no text layer. Recognition errors can damage both narration and document retrieval.

An OCR quality classifier can flag pages for human review using recognition confidence, unusual character frequency, and word statistics. A low confidence score alone is not a calibrated probability that a page is incorrect.

questions.question: Why does a scanned document need an extra extraction step?
Which signals could flag an unreadable page for review?

passages.text: A content-addressed audio cache hashes the provider, model, voice, and spoken text. A change to pronunciation changes the text and therefore the cache key.
A cache scoped to a user avoids revealing that another user has narrated the same content. A global cache requires a separate privacy analysis.

questions.question: Why should correcting pronunciation invalidate cached speech?
How does a private cache avoid leaking other users' activity?

passages.text: Dropout randomly disables some activations during neural network training. This reduces reliance on particular activations and can improve generalization. Dropout is disabled during ordinary inference.
Early stopping monitors validation performance and ends training when improvement stalls. The selected checkpoint should be chosen using validation data rather than the final test set.

questions.question: Is random activation masking used when serving a trained network?
What determines when early stopping should end training?

passages.text: Row level security enforces database access policies for each row. A document search query should run with the authenticated user's identity so it returns only passages they own.
A service role key bypasses row level security. It belongs in trusted server processes and should never be placed in a browser bundle or used for user-scoped retrieval.

questions.question: How can document search restrict evidence to the signed-in owner?
Why is an administrative database credential unsuitable for browser search?

unanswerable.question: What is the author's telephone number?
What was the exact cost of training these models?
